params.body:
A trend goes on gentells.com when it has seen it: at least five observations of its own.

On 2 October 21 of the 61 trends on the site rested on fewer than five things anyone posted, four on none: other people's reports, read back. Gentells sells what it saw.

- `decideShowcase(id, 'approved')` refuses a trend with fewer than `TW_SITE_MIN_OBSERVED` (default 5) observed signals (the Standard's evidence kind `observed`, i.e. platform signals), with the count in the reason: "Seen on platforms 1 time; a trend goes on gentells.com with at least 5 observations of its own." Both doors use it: the Studio's Curate and the curation mail. Skipping and hiding are always possible.
- The Curate queue (`/site/trends` pending) carries `observed` per trend, so the Studio can show it before anyone presses Approve.
- Trends already on the site are not touched: a search for their own observations runs first (widen-evidence, separate PR), and what stays empty after it is a decision for later.

`test/site-min-observed.test.mjs`; the older showcase tests, whose fixtures carry no signals, set the minimum to 0. 997 tests pass.
params.title: Showcase: at least five observations of its own
